title: Claude can tidy its notes between sessions. It can also save the wrong rule.
friendlyTitle: An AI can keep notes for next time, and those notes can be wrong
summary: Anthropic describes agent memory as notes kept between sessions, separate from weight changes and from summaries inside one chat. On a database task, a memory folder lifted Claude Opus 5.5's mean reward from 0.655 to 0.838; in Pokémon, Fable 5 kept about 10 files and earned four badges, while Sonnet 3.7 kept 413 files and earned one.
friendlySummary: Anthropic explains how Claude saves notes between chats, instead of trying to remember everything in one conversation. With a memory folder, a stronger Claude did better on a database task. A newer model also played further in a game by saving a few strategy notes, not hundreds of files.
whyItMatters: A saved rule is a prediction that it will still be true next time, and it can be wrong. Writing every screen detail can crowd out the task, so the useful habit is to keep tested rules and let idle 'dreaming' fix the rest.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A note is only a guess that the same fact will matter later. Save the rules you have checked, and do not treat a long memory file as proof the agent understood you.
